function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for drivers 21+.
• Lower limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Laws | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, turning, and highway exits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus resumes motion. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Maintain safe following distance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Pay for parking in designated areas. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspection required for most vehicles (except some exempt categories). | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance Requirements | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must use a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Motorcycles**: Must have a valid motorcycle endorsement.
• **Commercial Vehicles**: Additional regulations for trucks, buses, and hazardous materials. | Texas Transportation Code – Chapters 545, 546, 547 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDMV Website**: Regular updates on licensing, registration, and insurance requirements. - **TxDOT**: Roadway regulations, speed limits, and construction notices. - **Texas Legislature Online**: Access to the Texas Transportation Code and recent legislative changes. - **Local County Courts**: For specific traffic citations and court procedures. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. 2. **Avoid distractions** – no texting, no handheld phone use. 3. **Observe posted speed limits** – they can change at construction zones or in school districts. 4. **Be mindful of school buses** – stop and wait until the bus moves again. 5. **Check your insurance** – ensure you meet the minimum coverage requirements. If you need detailed statutes or have a specific scenario (e.g., a traffic ticket, insurance claim, or a particular road rule), let me know and I can dive deeper!
